title: Juniper Holdings KYC onramp stream
content:
Purpose: capture raw notes from discovery + first technical call with Juniper Holdings (compliance + product teams). Keep messy — this is the single-source scratchpad for SE + eng handoff.

Meeting recap (2024-10-20):
- Attendees: Juniper: Priya Shah (Head of Compliance), Omar Ruiz (SRE), Lina Park (Product). Redwood: Samira Khan, Marcus Lee.
- High-level ask: replace manual KYC intake pipeline with an LLM-assisted assistant that extracts entities, flags risk, and generates an adjudication summary. Must meet EMEA data residency and have auditable redaction steps.
- Deployment preference: Private (VPC) initially, option to migrate to Dedicated later. On-prem considered for higher-risk cohorts but not in MVP.

Key technical constraints / requirements:
- Data residency: all PII for EU customers must stay in the EU region; logs can be aggregated but must be encrypted with their KMS.
- Throughput/Latency: target 50 concurrent file uploads, 300ms median inference latency goal for short-text extraction path (entity extraction + confidence scores). For full adjudication summary (longer prompt + context) SLO 1.2s.
- Document types: bank statements (PDF scans), government IDs (JPEG/PNG), multi-page PDFs with OCR. Doc store: DocuVault (legacy), S3 for archived records.
- PII handling: they want deterministic redaction step pre-llm where SSNs, IBANs, tax ids are stripped and replaced with stable tokens. Need chain-of-custody audit trail.
- Explainability: compliance requires per-field provenance; must show which prompt/llm output produced a field and confidence.
- Model quality: high precision on DOB/Name extraction (>98) on scanned docs with moderate noise.

Gotchas & concerns (raw):
- Their OCR baseline is shaky — lots of noise from scanned faxes. Need to push for/experiment with alternate OCR (Tesseract post-process + small ml-based error correction) before relying on embeddings.
- Embedding-based matching for deduplication might falsely merge near-duplicates for common business names — threshold tuning required.
- Latency budget may be unrealistic for full PDF pipeline without batching + pre-cache; consider two-path architecture: fast-extract lightweight model + slower summary model.
- Encryption requirements: HSM-backed KMS only in EMEA region; Redwood Private must integrate with customer KMS keys. Verify our Private installer supports customer-supplied KMS (TODO: engineer confirmation).
- Audit logs: Priya stressed that logs must be tamper-evident; discuss options (append-only storage, signed audit entries).

Initial architecture sketch (informal):
1) Ingest: S3/DocuVault -> preprocessing queue. OCR stage (customer-provided engine OR Redwood-recommended pipeline).
2) Pre-redaction: PII regex + ML taggers -> tokenization (stable token mapping stored in encrypted vault).
3) Fast-extract path: small, quantized model (e.g., LLaMA-variant q4) for field-level extraction + confidence -> write to DB and emit event.
4) Summary path: larger model for adjudication summary (long-context, uses cached embeddings + KV cache in serving runtime); asynchronous, higher latency allowed.
5) Monitoring: Console dashboards for token-level cost, per-route latency, field-level accuracy regressions.

Open technical questions (assignments):
- Does Redwood Private composer support custom KMS ARNs in installer? (ASSIGN: Marcus)
- What OCR recommendations have other banking customers adopted for low-quality scans? Are there pre-built connectors? (ASSIGN: Samira to compile notes + share examples)
- Feasibility study for two-model path to meet 300ms median on extract path — quick perf run needed with representative PDFs. (ASSIGN: Eng perf team, ticket JIRA-2142)
- How to persist stable tokens for redaction while keeping them unlinkable outside the vault? Need SRE/security design review. (ASSIGN: Noah + Security)

Quick prompt prototypes (brain dump):
- "Extract name, DOB, ID types from the attached OCR text. For each field, return: field_name, value, character_span, confidence (0-1), source_page, provenance_token."
- For summary: "Based on extracted fields and document text, write a 3-sentence adjudication summary and list why each decision was made referencing evidence (page, line). Flag fields with confidence < 0.7."

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Field extraction precision/recall thresholds met on Juniper sample set (deliver eval harness).
- Redaction + tokenization pipeline in place with KMS encryption of mapping table.
- Runbook for fallback (if Private capacity constrained -> route to Dedicated EU region with no log export).
- Console dashboards for per-client latency and token spend.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Send meeting notes + ask for sample documents (Priya) — Samira (today).
- Kick-off perf run: Eng to spin synthetic PDFs and test extract model latency (Marcus -> JIRA-2142, due 2024-11-01).
- Security sync: schedule 30m with Redwood Security to confirm KMS/HSM options + audit-log guarantees (Noah to schedule).
- Draft SOW outline for Private deployment + support hours needed for on-prem installer (Samira to produce draft and share w/ pricing).

Loose ideas / exploration (low priority):
- Pre-cook embeddings for recurring customers to speed up adjudication (cache per-client recent transcripts).
- Local-only redaction microservice (runs in customer subnet) to minimize exposure of raw PII to Redwood systems.
- Use lightweight rule-based prefilter to reduce calls to larger models (cost control).

Notes to self: be conservative in promises around latency for scanned PDFs. Emphasize test-driven approach (we need their sample set). Keep compliance team close — they will gate anything that touches raw IDs.

Raw action log (for handoff):
- 2024-10-21 Samira: sent note asking for sample docs + compliance checklist.
- 2024-10-22 Priya: replied, will share redaction policy + sample bundle by 2024-10-25.
- 2024-10-23 Marcus: started perf-run plan (JIRA-2142).

End of scratchpad — convert to more formal handoff doc after we get samples and perf results.
summary: Discovery scratchpad for Juniper Holdings KYC onramp: private deployment, OCR and redaction constraints, two-path architecture proposed (fast extract + summary), KMS + audit-log concerns, action items assigned (Marcus, Noah, Samira), next steps: sample docs, perf runs, security sync.
